title: Paloma and the Witness
premise: When insurance investigator Rafael Montrose receives a confession letter for the drowning of Paloma Reyes—a case closed seven years ago—the letter is postmarked the day after the victim's mother's funeral, and signed with Rafael's own childhood nickname. Haunted by gaps in their otherwise flawless memory of that night, Rafael reopens the file and discovers the town of Salt Hollow built its quiet prosperity on a lie they all agreed to keep. As the letter writer begins sending pages of the truth one by one, Rafael must decide whether exposing the conspiracy that includes their own family is worth destroying the only belonging they've ever known. The ending reveals Rafael witnessed the drowning as a child and buried it; the final chapter forces them to testify, trading the town's acceptance for the truth—and finding, in exile, a self worth belonging to.
about_author: Xanthe Dunmore is the pen name of a former coastal-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's secrets before turning to fiction. Their debut draws on small-town insurance fraud cases and the quiet violence of communities that protect their own.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Seven days after Elena Reyes's funeral, Rafael receives a confession to Paloma's drowning, signed 'Palomita'—the name only Rafael's late mother used for the dead girl. The emotional beat is dread: the letter writer knows something Rafael has spent seven years refusing to remember.

chapters.title: The Alphabetized Town
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael pulls the cold file and notices their own photographic memory has a seven-minute hole from the night Paloma died—the only gap in a lifetime of perfect recall. Interviews with the sheriff and the harbormaster yield rehearsed answers. Beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, 2016. Flashback: seventeen-year-old Paloma, a migrant cannery worker, witnesses the Voss family's boat smuggling undocumented laborers—and a fatal accident at the pier. She writes it all down, planning to send it to the insurance office. Beat: hopeful, doomed innocence.

chapters.title: A Second Page Arrives
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A second letter arrives containing Paloma's actual journal page, matching the confession word for word. Rafael's mother's handwriting appears in the margin of the copy. Beat: betrayal—the first person Rafael trusted was already inside the cover-up.

chapters.title: The Voss Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael breaks into the shuttered cannery office and finds a double ledger: the Voss family insured their own 'accidents,' collecting on deaths like Paloma's. Sheriff Deane catches Rafael there and warns them off with a kindness that feels like a threat. Beat: fear wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rafael interviews the surviving witnesses—each one reveals a piece of the pact: jobs, silence, hush-money checks cashed for years. Paloma's flashback shows her hiding the journal inside the church hymnal rack the night she died. Beat: the town's loyalty revealed as a debt everyone owes.

chapters.title: The Nickname
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael confronts the letter writer: it's Father Anselmo, dying of cancer, who found the journal while preparing Elena's funeral—and who knows Rafael was on the pier that night. He gives Rafael the final page but refuses to say what's on it. Beat: the past closing in.

chapters.title: Seven Minutes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, final flashback. The missing seven minutes: young Rafael saw the Voss patriarch push Paloma from the pier; their mother, the Vosses' bookkeeper, made Rafael forget by making the memory shameful instead of criminal. Beat: heartbreak—Rafael's perfect memory was never broken, only bargained away.

chapters.title: The Hearing at Salt Hollow
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the reopened inquest, Rafael testifies with total recall while the town watches from the pews—Deane resigns mid-hearing, the Voss heir storms out, and Rafael's own name appears in the ledger as a paid beneficiary. Beat: the climax—truth spoken at the cost of everything.

chapters.title: Palomita
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, epilogue. Months later, Rafael has left Salt Hollow, working claims in a city where no one knows their name. They mail the recovered journal to Paloma's cousin across the border and finally speak the nickname aloud at an unmarked grave. Beat: bittersweet resolution—belonging lost, self reclaimed.
